titulo: Indirect object pronouns: Me, te, le, nos, os, les

aula.objetivo: Use indirect object pronouns (me, te, le, nos, os, les) with verbs like dar, decir, escribir, regalar, prestar, and preguntar, distinguish the direct object from the indirect object, and avoid false friends like «apellido», «pegar», «prestar», and «regalar».

sessao.titulo: Me, te, le, nos, os, les

blocos.titulo: Le, les, and the other indirect object pronouns
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: the indirect object answers the question «to whom?» or «for whom?» after the verb. In «Doy un libro a Ana», I give the book to whom? To Ana. The book is the direct object; Ana is the indirect object. STEP 2: the indirect object pronouns are «me» (me), «te» (you, tú), «le» (him, her, usted), «nos» (us), «os» (you-all, vosotros), and «les» (them, ustedes). Only the third person differs from the direct object of lesson 23: here it's «le, les», and there it was «lo, la, los, las». STEP 3: «le» and «les» don't change for gender: «Le doy un libro» works for «a ella» and for «a él». STEP 4: the position is the same as the direct object: before the conjugated verb («Le escribo») or attached to the infinitive («Quiero escribirle»). STEP 5: the pronoun shows up even when the person's name is also in the sentence: «Le doy el libro a Ana», «Les escribo a mis padres». That isn't redundancy — it's simply the normal way to speak. STEP 6: for emphasis or contrast, add «a mí», «a ti», «a él», «a ella», «a usted», «a nosotros», «a vosotros», «a ellos», «a ustedes»: «A mí me dio un libro y a ti no». STEP 7: an English speaker tends to translate "to her" literally and reach for just «a ella», leaving out the pronoun: «Dije a ella». The correct form always keeps the pronoun too: «le dije». STEP 8: the same pronouns show up with «gustar», which you've already seen: «A Ana le gusta el té» and «Me gusta el té».
blocos.comparacao: English marks the indirect object with word order instead of a required pronoun: «I gave her the book» or «I gave the book to her» both work, and the sentence is complete without any extra marker once "her" appears. Spanish never drops that marker: «le di el libro» keeps «le» in place even though «a ella» may also be stated outright, so the habit of skipping the pronoun once the person is already named — which feels natural in English — has to be unlearned for Spanish.

exemplos.ru: Le regalé un libro a mi hermana.
exemplos.pt: I gave my sister a book as a gift.

exemplos.ru: Les dije la verdad a mis padres.
exemplos.pt: I told my parents the truth.
I want to show you a photo.
Will you lend me the charger?

tabela.exemplo: [misto] Le explico la regla a Ana.

erros.motivo: In Spanish, the indirect object becomes a pronoun placed before the verb.
«Les» is only for plural; «mi madre» is singular.
The pronoun comes before the conjugated verb, with no hyphen.

erros.errado: [misto] Le doy los libros a mis amigos.
erros.certo: [misto] Les doy los libros a mis amigos.
erros.motivo: When the person is plural, the pronoun is plural too.

erros.errado: [misto] Yo dijo a ti la verdad.
erros.motivo: Use «te» for «a ti», and the form «dije» for «yo».

blocos.enunciado: Say out loud what you gave, said, or wrote to five people (your mother, a friend, a colleague, a neighbor, a teacher), using «le» or «les». Example: «Le regalé un libro a mi hermana.»
Answer using a pronoun: «¿Compraste el pan?», «¿Ves a Ana?», «¿Tienes las llaves?», «¿Me esperas?»
